content:
Manchester United have confirmed the high-profile arrival of Manuel Ugarte from Paris Saint-Germain, securing the Uruguayan midfielder for a fee of €50m (£42m) with a further €10m in achievable bonuses. Ugarte, who is just 23 years old, signed a five-year contract with an option to extend by a further year, emphasizing the club’s long-term faith in his abilities. The move is considered a significant reinforcement for manager Erik ten Hag, who has been focused on strengthening the squad’s backbone as he looks to restore the club’s former glory.

Ugarte, known for his determined and competitive edge, expressed his pride and excitement at joining such a prestigious organization. Speaking on his unveiling, he shared: “It is an incredible feeling to join a club of this magnitude – one that is admired all around the world. The project that the football leadership discussed with me is extremely exciting. Manchester United is an ambitious club and I am an ambitious player.” His words resonated with fans, eager for a revival following recent seasons of inconsistency.

He continued, “I know how incredible United fans are and I cannot wait to experience Old Trafford. I’m someone who is so determined to succeed. I will sacrifice and give everything for my teammates. Together we will fight to win trophies and reach the level where this club needs to be.” The midfield dynamo brings a reputation for relentless energy and commitment, attributes that could prove decisive as United aim for success on all fronts.

From the management side, Dan Ashworth, United’s new sporting director, highlighted the significance of the acquisition: “Signing Manuel was another of our primary targets for this summer. His style and drive fit perfectly with our vision for the team, and we are thrilled to welcome him to Manchester.” With Ugarte joining as the fifth major addition during this transfer window, it’s evident that the club is serious in its efforts to build a squad capable of challenging for major honours.

Supporters will now be waiting excitedly to see Ugarte in action, anticipating the impact he can bring alongside experienced figures like Casemiro. With this latest move, Manchester United hope to usher in a new era, marked by renewed ambition and a hunger for silverware.

Any other questions?
